subject: math

objective.text: Use place value to multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000 without drawing every step.

explanations.title: Left is ten times larger
explanations.text: Moving one place left makes a unit ten times larger. Moving one place right makes it one tenth as large.

explanations.title: Zeros tell the shift
explanations.text: Multiply by one hundred and every digit moves two places left. There are two zeros in one hundred. Divide by one hundred and the digits move two places right.

explanations.title: Think about the unit
explanations.text: The digits in 4.3 times ten are the same as in 4.3. Only the units change. 43 tenths and 4 ones 3 tenths are the same amount.

hints.text: Draw the place value chart. Put each digit in its own place.
Multiplying by ten moves every digit one place to the left. Dividing moves it right.
Count the zeros in the number you multiply or divide by. That tells how many places the digits move.
The exponent tells how many tens are multiplied together. It matches the zeros.
Say the unit name. Then use a basic fact with that unit.
Think how many small units fit in a big unit. Then multiply or divide.
Add or subtract like units. Tenths with tenths, hundredths with hundredths.
Trade ten of a small unit for one of the next larger unit.
Compare digits from the left. Find the first place where they differ.
Rename both numbers with the same unit. Then compare.
Find the nearest numbers on each side for that place. Then check if you are past the halfway point.
Round the numbers and estimate first. Then place the decimal point.
Draw an area model. Multiply each unit by the whole number. Then add the partial products.
If you cannot share a unit evenly, trade it for ten of the next smaller unit.
Draw a tape diagram. Label the total and the parts.
Divide like whole numbers first. Then think about the unit to place the decimal point.

Source is Eureka Math / EngageNY, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (Great Minds). Cards made from it must credit Great Minds, stay non-commercial, and share under the same license. Check this before any paid deployment.

The lesson file is plain text with NO page images and NO page numbers. Fraction symbols, tape diagrams, number bonds and figures were lost in the text, so student answers such as 'S: [blank]' cannot be read. Only fractions written in words (for example '5 sixths') were used. Compare every question with the original PDF.
Diffusion cannot be trusted for counts or fractions. Use code-rendered visuals for anything with exact numbers, and have a person check each visual against the answer key.
Prerequisites that start with math_g5_m1_ point to earlier cards of this module made in the same project. Check that each earlier lesson really teaches the needed skill.

Hint coverage is thin. Hints come from the lesson's teaching moves.
Single-answer items have no real partial outcome. The script must map partial to the same path as incorrect, or the shared schema must allow null.
All 2 assets are marked not_available (a_pv_chart, a_number_line). Each has a visual spec. Items that use them cannot launch until the asset exists.

The source is a teacher script for a 60-minute class with partners and objects. All child-facing text was rewritten for a screen and fractions are written in words. Needs an age-appropriate wording review.
The file has no page numbers and no version footer. Every page is 'n/a' and the section name is used instead. source_version is 'not stated in file'. Fill in from the original PDF.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
